title: Customer Network Guardrails Playbook (Mini PRD)
summary: A compact PRD that defines a lightweight guardrails set for customer-managed networking onboarding and runbook-grade audit/logging defaults. Focused on creating a friction-minimized path for customers to connect private VPCs while capturing minimal forensic signals to satisfy SOC audits and incident response without blowing retention budgets.
goals: 1) Provide a short, defensible baseline of audit events for private deployments (connection lifecycle + approval provenance). 2) Ship self-service approval presets so small customers can onboard without engineering support. 3) Offer operator-facing quickchecks and a 3-step rollback recipe for common connectivity failures. 4) Keep default retention cheap: 90-day active, 365-day compact indexes, with sampling heuristics for long tails.
non_goals: Not a full attestation ledger or immutable evidence vault. Not implementing enterprise HSM-backed receipts in this mini-PRD. Not attempting to solve every global jurisdiction retention policy (we provide hooks for per-customer overrides).
requirements: Functional: capture connection events (create/update/delete), approval decisions (actor, role, decision, rationale), keystore operations (rotate, escrow), and operator actions (rollback, emergency-bypass). Non-functional: event write latency <=100ms p99, availability 99.9 for audit ingestion pipeline, per-tenant sampling and compression configurable, and exportable compact evidence bundles for customer export. UX: approval presets with three profiles (fast-start, validated, locked-down); clear operator checklists surfaced in Console.
user_flow_overview: 1) Customer initiates private VPC handshake via Console or API. 2) System collects a connection bundle and triggers an approval flow per preset. 3) Approval decision recorded; if 'auto-approve' preset chosen, connection proceeds and an audit event marks the path. 4) Runtime telemetry and connection heartbeats stream to an ephemeral cache. 5) Operator Console shows quickchecks; on anomaly operator can execute rollback or request revalidation.
audit_event_schema: Event fields (minimal): event_id, ts_utc, tenant_id, event_type, actor_id, actor_role, outcome, rationale, related_object (type/id), snapshot_hash (optional), sampling_tag. Examples: CONNECTION_CREATED, APPROVAL_GRANTED, APPROVAL_ESCALATED, KEY_ROTATED, OPERATOR_ROLLBACK. Keep schema flat and extensible. Use compact JSON lines; retention policy metadata attached as headers in the storage layer.
approval_gates: Three presets: 1) Fast-start: auto-approve for pre-validated customers; minimal justification stored. 2) Team-validated: requires at least one operator with 'network-admin' role to sign-off; stores rationale text. 3) Regulated: multi-actor, time-bound approvals with explicit evidence snapshot. All gates support optional escalation rules (timeout -> human review) and emergency bypass that leaves a high-fidelity audit trace and requires post-facto attestation.
operator_checklist: Pre-apply: verify CIDR non-overlap, validate peering ACL, confirm KMS key presence. Post-apply quickchecks (3): ping control-plane endpoint from customer az, confirm metrics ingestion (heartbeats within 60s), validate audit event receipt. Failure path: if heartbeat missing -> run connection health script, if audit missing -> check ingestion queue and trigger exporter fallback. If serious, run rollback recipe.
rollback_recipe: 1) Trigger graceful drain: stop new sessions and mark endpoint draining. 2) Revoke new connection tokens and re-issue to previous known-good config. 3) Publish incident note and attach the compact evidence bundle (last 30 minutes). 4) If rollback fails, escalate to SRE and open a forensics ticket with required artifacts (snapshot_hashes, timeline, operator_actions).
metrics_and_slos: Ingestion latency p95 < 30ms, p99 < 100ms. Audit event durability: write success >= 99.99%. Console quickchecks time-to-surface < 5s from ingestion. Onboarding success rate goal: 90% for fast-start preset in first 30 minutes. Cost guardrail: average audit storage per active tenant < 50MB/month at default sampling.
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal test tenants + 3 pilot customers (4 weeks). Beta: open to broader self-serve with opt-in 'fast-start' (8 weeks). GA: presets enabled by default but with clear guidance and billing opt-in for extended retention (12+ weeks). Provide migration tool for customers with custom retention to map to compact index format.
privacy_and_compliance_notes: Default captures minimal PII; actor_id can be hashed for storage. Provide hooks for customers to require PI redaction or to opt for full-evidence exports for their auditors. Retention overrides require explicit contract addendum beyond default cheap tier.
open_questions: 1) Should 'emergency bypass' require a signed cryptographic receipt or is a high-fidelity audit trace sufficient? 2) What thresholds should trigger automatic sampling reduction for noisy tenants? 3) How to align compact evidence bundle format with legal e-discovery requests across jurisdictions?
next_steps: 1) Align with Legal on retention tiers and wording (owner: Reema). 2) Prototype event ingestion with compact-lines in serving-runtime (owner: Daniel). 3) Build Console quickcheck mock and test operator checklist with SRE roleplay (owner: Liam). 4) Schedule pilot kickoff with two customers in Feb 2025.
notes: This mini-PRD intentionally keeps scope small: key deliverable is a hardened baseline that lets engineers and customers move through VPC handshakes safely while providing auditors and SREs enough signal to act. If pilots surface larger attestation needs, escalate to a full PRD for an immutable evidence ledger.
references: See linked Confluence page PD-1221 for deeper background, Jira PD-7842 for tickets, and the experimental exporter PR in GitHub for ingestion format examples.
